title: RBACv2 Key Access Attestation and SIEM Enrichment
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures a practical pattern for combining RBAC v2-driven key access attestations with an enriched SIEM ingestion schema and automated evidence exports. It is intended for: security engineers, compliance owners, platform SREs, and teams operating BYOK/HSM integrations. The approach here is implementation-agnostic but includes concrete audit-field names and suggested SIEM queries to standardize downstream alerting and reporting.

Why this is different: we treat KMS access as first-class authorization events (RBAC assertions), not just KMS-native logs. That lets us tie key operations directly to role grants, policy changes, and attestation windows for rotation and escrow flows.

High-level design:

1) Event model: unify three sources into a single canonical audit stream:
   - RBAC v2 decision records (allow/deny with policy hash)
   - KMS/HSM operation logs (import, wrap, unwrap, sign, decrypt, rotate, destroy)
   - Evidence automation exports (signed snapshots of key metadata, rotation receipts)

2) Canonical audit record fields (flat schema, required names):
   - event_id: string UUID
   - event_ts: ISO8601 timestamp
   - principal_id: user/service principal identifier (email or service-id)
   - principal_type: human | service | system
   - rbac_policy_id: short id or hash (from RBAC v2 policy store)
   - rbac_decision: allow | deny | conditional
   - decision_reason: short string (e.g., "policy:allow-for-role:key-admin")
   - action: kms.create | kms.import | kms.rotate | kms.wrap | kms.unwrap | kms.decrypt | kms.encrypt | kms.destroy | kms.update-policy
   - key_id: canonical key resource name (projects/…/keys/ID)
   - key_variant: tenant-managed | redwood-managed | byok | hsm-wrapped
   - key_version: semantic version or key version id
   - operation_result: success | partial | failure
   - result_code: numeric or string error code
   - client_ip: IP or NATed IP (if available)
   - agent: sdk-name/version or operator cli (e.g., redwood-sdk-python/2.1.0)
   - request_id: upstream request UUID (correlate to trace)
   - trace_id: distributed trace id (if present)
   - evidence_artifact: signed-url-or-id (for automated snapshot exports)
   - retention_tier: hot | warm | archive

3) RBAC v2 attestation enrichment rules:
   - On sensitive actions (wrap/unwrap/import/rotate/destroy), attach a fresh attestation token that proves the decision was evaluated against RBAC v2 store at event_ts with policy_hash and policy_version fields.
   - Attestation token must be signed by policy-service KMS and include: principal_id, role_bindings_snapshot_id, evaluated_policy_hash, evaluation_time, ttl.
   - Store the attestation token location in evidence_artifact and index its fingerprint in the SIEM (attestation_fingerprint).

Rotation and escrow procedure (operational playbook):

Pre-rotation checks (owner: platform-crypto, runbook id: ROT-PL-03):
  - Confirm rotation window (start/end) published to incident-ops calendar and customer tenants notified (if BYOK)
  - Snapshot key metadata (current versions, usage stats for last 90d) and export signed snapshot to evidence bucket
  - Run RBAC audit to list principals with wrap/unwrap privileges; export that list as part of attestation package
  - Ensure HSM health checks pass (latency, temperature, error counters) and that HSM fallback pool is available

Rotation steps (canary-first):
  - 00: Prepare canary key version (create new key version or import wrapped blob into HSM)
  - 05: Deploy canary route for <1% traffic or internal test workload; monitor decrypt success rate and latency for 30m
  - 35: If canary passes, schedule phased rollout across regions/tenants in waves (configurable), with automatic rollback on failure thresholds
  - 45: Emit rotation-complete audit record including prior_version, new_version, rotation_job_id, and attach attestation token

Post-rotation verification:
  - Export signed rotation receipt (artifact) and index into SIEM (artifact_id). Retention policy: keep hot for 90d, archive for 10y for regulated tenants.
  - Run automated validation queries to detect any clients still referencing deprecated versions and create tickets for owners

HSM failover and BYOK considerations:
  - For BYOK, maintain escrow policy: escrow only encrypted wrapping blobs (never plaintext) and require dual control: operator + customer key-unlock share.
  - HSM fallback: when primary HSM cluster is unhealthy, rotate traffic to a compatible HSM with same crypto module profile. Emit a "hsm-failover" event in canonical audit stream with hsm_cluster_from and hsm_cluster_to and attach operator approval record.

SIEM enrichment and example queries:

Enrichment best-practices:
  - Index attestation_fingerprint, rbac_policy_id, key_variant, operation_result, principal_type, and evidence_artifact as top-level fields
  - Normalize request_id and trace_id to correlate KMS activity to API gateway traces and runtime logs
  - Tag BYOK operations with tenant_id and attach signed customer consent artifact id

Example SIEM rule (pseudo-KQL):
  - Detect suspicious key export attempts:
    source=canonical_kms_stream action in ("kms.unwrap", "kms.export", "kms.import") and principal_type=="service" and (rbac_decision=="allow" and decision_reason not contains "scheduled-rotation") | where operation_result!="success" or (action=="kms.unwrap" and client_ip not in trusted_nat_ranges)

Evidence automation pipeline (sketch):
  - exporter-service subscribes to canonical audit stream (pub/sub)
  - For each sensitive event, exporter assembles payload: canonical_record + attestation_token + signed_snapshot (if rotation/import) and writes to evidence-bucket with multipart-signed manifest
  - A separate service (evidence-indexer) reads the bucket and writes a compact index record to SIEM and to archival DB (immutable ledger)
  - Retention/crypto: evidence objects encrypted with evidence-KMS; evidence-KMS keys are rotated on a separate cadence and have stronger dual-control policies

Audit queries and compliance checks (operational recipes):
  - "Key access by human admins in last 30d" -> filter principal_type==human and action in (wrap, unwrap, rotate, destroy)
  - "Rotation evidence completeness" -> every rotation_job_id must have 3 artifacts: (snapshot, attestation-token, rotation-receipt); missing -> create SEC-TICKET auto
  - "RBAC policy drift" -> compute policy_hash over time and alert if assignment lists changed without a recorded change request (Confluence or JIRA link required)

Open questions / risks / TODOs:
  - How do we minimize noise from high-frequency service principals that legitimately call wrap/unwrap many times per minute? (need rate-bucketed alerting)
  - Evidence artifact retention for non-US tenants with different legal holds — build tenant-aware retention plugin
  - Performance cost: attaching attestation tokens on every KMS call may add latency; consider async attestation for non-sensitive reads

Operational checklists (quick):
  - Onboarding BYOK tenant: verify customer public key fingerprint, verify escrow policy consent, record tenant_id in evidence-index
  - Pre-rotation: create JIRA ticket ROT-<tenant>-<date> and attach RBAC export and signed snapshot
  - Incident: on any unexpected key destroy, immediately disable all key usage via routing policy, initiate legal hold export, and run forensic query: source=canonical_kms_stream action=="kms.destroy" | where event_ts > <window>

Notes:
  - This doc is a working draft. Next steps: prototype attestation token format (compact JWT with policy hash claim), implement proof-of-concept exporter that appends attestation_fingerprint into Elastic ingest pipeline, and run two rotations with canary flows to validate end-to-end evidence capture.
